caption: Aspen grove in winter near Clearwater, BC. Ruffed grouse eat aspen buds all winter.
author: Jason Hollinger

caption: Black bear standing in a fall berry patch. Bears follow the ripening fruit.
author: U. S. Fish and Wildlife Service - Northeast Region

caption: Claw marks on an aspen trunk where a bear climbed.
author: GlacierNPS
cardBack: Bear claw marks: parallel scratches on smooth aspen bark where a bear climbed.

caption: Black bear scat full of berries, with a pen for scale.
author: USFWSmidwest
cardBack: Bear scat full of berries: a berry patch nearby is in use.

caption: Black bear scat on a trail in Mission Park, Kelowna. Full of seeds and skins.
author: Accuruss

caption: Black bear front track in the Pasayten, next to the Okanagan. Wide pad, 5 toes.
author: vhhammer
cardBack: Black bear front track: wide pad, 5 toes in an arc.

caption: Black bear track in mud. The hind foot looks a little like a human foot.
author: ShenandoahNPS

caption: Beaver lodge on a pond with ducks. Beaver ponds are duck ponds.
author: Greenbilly

caption: Bitterbrush up close. Tiny wedge shaped leaves with 3 teeth at the tip.
author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
cardBack: Bitterbrush: grey green dry slope shrub, tiny wedge leaves with 3 teeth. Key mule deer browse.

caption: Bitterbrush in bloom along a dry pine slope, Nevada. Same shrub as the Okanagan.
author: USFWS Pacific Southwest Region

caption: Himalayan blackberry thicket. Cover for deer and bears on Fraser Valley edges.
author: Thayne Tuason
cardBack: Himalayan blackberry: thorny tangles on Fraser Valley edges. Cover for deer and bears.

caption: Bracken fern on a cut block edge.
author: brewbooks from near Seattle, USA
cardBack: Bracken fern: big triangle fronds on cut blocks and edges.

caption: Cattail head: a brown sausage on a stalk. It shouts "marsh" from 500 m.
author: Terry.grignon
cardBack: Cattail: brown sausage head, tall flat leaves. Marsh cover for ducks.

caption: Cattail marsh. Tall flat leaves; ducks hide and nest in it.
author: Chris Light

caption: Snowbrush leaf: glossy, sticky, 3 strong veins from the base.
author: Thayne Tuason
cardBack: Snowbrush ceanothus: glossy sticky leaves with 3 veins from the base. Sprouts after fire. Deer browse.

caption: Snowbrush on an open slope. Shiny leaves, white flower clusters in early summer.
author: Matt Lavin

caption: Chokecherry in fruit. Brushy draws with berries hold quail and grouse.
author: Thayne Tuason
cardBack: Chokecherry: dark red to black cherries in hanging clusters. Grouse, quail and bear food.

caption: Fresh deer pellets: dark, shiny and moist.
author: Steve Redman ( MORA )
cardBack: Deer pellets, fresh: dark, shiny, moist. About 1 to 1.5 cm long.

caption: Old deer pellets: dry, pale and crumbly.
author: Rosendahl

caption: A buck rub: bark stripped from a small tree at knee to waist height.
author: Wasp32
cardBack: Buck rub: bark stripped from a sapling at knee to waist height, late summer to the rut.

caption: Deer track near Wenatchee, Washington, in dry ground like the Okanagan. Two pointed toes.
author: Thayne Tuason
cardBack: Deer track: split heart, pointed end forward, about 5 to 9 cm.

caption: Deer track in soft soil. The split heart shape points the way the deer walked.
author: Thayne Tuason

caption: A deer trail pushed through grass. Packed soil and tracks in the middle.
author: MaryC2000

caption: Deer tracks on a snowy trail. One line, prints close together: walking.
author: Peter Cooper Jr.

caption: Red osier dogwood in flower. Its white berries feed grouse in fall.
author: Robert Flogaus-Faust

caption: Red osier dogwood in a wet draw. Red stems stand out after the leaves drop.
author: Matt Lavin
cardBack: Red osier dogwood: red stems, wet ground. Favourite fall and winter browse for deer and moose.

caption: Interior Douglas fir stand. Thick old trees make shade in fall and shelter in snow.
author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA

caption: A lone Douglas fir on a dry grass slope. Soft needles, thick furrowed bark.
author: Matt Lavin
cardBack: Douglas fir: soft flat needles, thick bark, cones with 3 pointed bracts. Winter food and thermal cover.

caption: Webbed tracks in mud: 3 forward toes joined by skin.
author: Ryan Hodnett
cardBack: Duck track: 3 forward toes joined by webbing.

caption: Elk pellets in a meadow. Bigger than deer pellets, with a boot for scale.
author: Una Smith
cardBack: Elk pellets: bigger than deer pellets, often in large piles in meadows.

caption: Subalpine fir rubbed raw by a bull elk. Bark stripped high up the trunk.
author: Loren Lane ( MORA )

caption: Elk tracks churning a lake shore where a herd came to drink.
author: Loren Lane ( MORA )

caption: Elk trail in spring snow: many animals walking in single file.
author: Loren Lane ( MORA )

caption: Elk wallow: a muddy pit in a wet meadow, dug and rolled in by bulls in the rut.
author: Loren Lane ( MORA )
cardBack: Elk wallow: muddy pit dug and rolled in by bulls in the September rut.

caption: Geese feeding in corn stubble in snow. Fraser Valley fields look like this in winter.
author: Andrea_44 from Leamington, Ontario , Canada

caption: The edge: grass meets Douglas fir. Deer feed in the open and bed in the trees.
author: Andres Alvarado

caption: Snow roost hole with wing marks. A ruffed grouse burst out of here.
author: Cephas
cardBack: Grouse snow roost: hole in soft snow with wing marks where the bird burst out.

caption: A grouse track line: 3 forward toes, one print in front of the next.
author: NPS
cardBack: Grouse track: 3 long toes forward, short one back, about 5 cm.

caption: Ruffed grouse tracks winding through soft snow.
author: Yellowstone National Park

caption: Wing prints in the snow where a grouse took off or landed.
author: John Good

caption: Black huckleberry. Bears fatten on these in August and September.
author: julie from Idaho, united states
cardBack: Black huckleberry: dark purple berry, thin oval leaves. Bear food in August and September.

caption: Huckleberry shrubs on a rocky ridge. Late summer food for dusky grouse.
author: Katja Schulz from Washington, D. C., USA

caption: Pond, hay fields and cottonwoods near Kamloops. Water, food and shelter close together.
author: cogdogblog

caption: Sagebrush slope on the Mara trail, Kamloops. Grey shrubs, bare soil between.
author: Ghune

caption: Kinnikinnick, a low mat with red berries on dry, rocky ground under pine and fir.
author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
cardBack: Kinnikinnick: low evergreen mat, spoon shaped leaves, red berries. Dry open ground.

caption: Lac du Bois grassland north of Kamloops in October. Open bunchgrass, few trees.
author: tuchodi

caption: Rolling grassland with small pothole lakes and fir patches on the ridges.
author: Straitgate

caption: Moose tracks in mud. Much bigger than deer, with long pointed toes.
author: USFWS Mountain-Prairie
cardBack: Moose track: about 13 to 15 cm, more than twice a deer track.

caption: A moose trail ploughed through deep snow among small spruce.
author: NPS staff

caption: Cow moose browsing willows in winter. Twig ends bitten off at chest height.
author: Yellowstone National Park from Yellowstone NP, USA

caption: Burned slope above the North Thompson River near Barriere. New green feed grows under the snags.
author: Adam Jones

caption: Haynes Point wetland on Osoyoos Lake. Reeds and calm water out of the wind.
author: B&B-Traveller

caption: Floating pondweed. Oval leaves on the surface, seed spikes above.
author: Christian Fischer
cardBack: Floating pondweed: oval leaves on the surface. Ducks eat seeds and plants.

caption: California quail cock near Vernon. Quail perch on a post or stump to watch for danger.
author: Alan D. Wilson

caption: Big sagebrush. Silver grey, smells strong when you crush a leaf.
author: Z3lvs
cardBack: Big sagebrush: silver grey, strong smell. Marks dry, low winter country.

caption: Salal, the shrub that covers the coast forest floor. Thick oval leaves.
author: Robert Flogaus-Faust
cardBack: Salal: thick oval leathery leaves, white bell flowers. Coast forest floor. Black tailed deer food.

caption: Salmonberry. Orange or red berries in early summer, wet ground.
author: Walter Siegmund (talk)
cardBack: Salmonberry: raspberry like orange or red berry, wet coast ground. Spring and summer deer food.

caption: Saskatoon berries forming in early summer on a dry slope.
author: Thayne Tuason

caption: Saskatoon in flower, Manning Park BC. White starry flowers, oval toothed leaves.
author: Robert Flogaus-Faust
cardBack: Saskatoon: oval leaves toothed on the top half, white spring flowers, purple July berries. Top deer browse.

caption: Skunk cabbage in a wet spring forest near Aldergrove. Early spring bear food.
author: The Cosmonaut
cardBack: Western skunk cabbage: yellow hood in wet spring forest. Early spring bear food.

caption: Snowberry. White berries that hang on into winter.
author: NPS Photo
cardBack: Snowberry: low shrub, round leaves, white berries that last into winter.

caption: Soopolallie (soapberry) with red berries, North Thompson River Park.
author: Robert Flogaus-Faust
cardBack: Soopolallie: opposite leaves, rusty undersides, red berries in July and August. Bear food.

caption: Subalpine forest of spruce and lodgepole pine, Manning Park. Spruce grouse country.
author: Tim Gage at Flickr

caption: Old cut block near Trophy Meadows, Wells Gray area. Young trees, shrubs and grass on the edges.
author: Jason Hollinger

caption: Willow shrub in a wet mountain meadow. Long narrow leaves, many stems.
author: Matt Lavin from Bozeman, Montana, USA
cardBack: Willow: many stems, long narrow leaves, wet ground. Top moose browse.

caption: Wild rose hips in fall. Red, oval, on thorny stems.
author: Jim Morefield from Nevada, USA
cardBack: Wild rose: thorny stems, red hips into winter. Deer, grouse and bears eat the hips.

caption: Wild rose along a dry creek. Thorny thickets are quail hiding cover.
author: Thayne Tuason
